title: MTHFR and Methylation: A Critical Insight for Health Practitioners | MTHFR Support Australia
abstract: # MTHFR and Methylation: A Critical Insight for Health Practitioners. One of the most critical yet overlooked biochemical pathways is **methylation**, a process that affects detoxification, DNA repair, immune function, neurotransmitter balance, fertility and cardiovascular health. Central to the methylation process is the **MTHFR (methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase) enzyme**, which plays a key role in folate metabolism and homocysteine regulation [1]. When the methylation cycle is impaired due to MTHFR polymorphisms, it can significantly impact a patient’s ability to maintain homeostasis, detoxify effectively, and regulate inflammation [3]. Clinical evidence suggests that patients with MTHFR mutations benefit from **methylated folate (5-MTHF) supplementation over folic acid** to bypass enzymatic limitations and support methylation pathways [8]. While genetic polymorphisms like MTHFR can predispose patients to certain health conditions,however, **epigenetic factors—including diet, stress, environmental toxin exposure, and lifestyle—play a crucial role in gene expression** [10]. If you think methylation is just about MTHFR and folate, think again.
